items.text:
Now a little more Linux Friendly

Returning users from the original google doc, should go through the First Time Setup again. I promise this is the last time, and is required for proper following of the guides.

“What are the benefits of replacing audio with Events instead of just using this image/svg+xml image/svg+xml ?”

Some of the more “simple” mods can use the PD3AudioModder tool, like replacing some small sound effects in the game. But some audio can have some strict expectations and can play weird/cut off with just simply replacing the audio directly without Wwise Events, or can even be impossible because of the way audio is handled in Papaya 3.

With Event replacing, the audio can be as long as you want and can be fancy with transitions, strict list of audio to play, sequences, control of which audio to play randomly, and potentially more!

It will also have the advantage of making mods smaller in size with compression methods built into wwise unreal integration, and not needing to have the same audio file copied several times to replace multiple audio sounds.

items.title: Work Unit Download
items.text:
Download this Work Unit:

Bulldozer SFX.wwu

Open the project's directory and locate the "Actor-Mixer Hierarchy" folder. You want to place the downloaded Work Unit inside this folder.

Now open the Wwise Project. If the Project was already opened, it may prompt to refresh/restart the app.

items.title: Event(s)
items.text:
Go into the Events tab. The following image of Events3 is required* to be made, in order to replace the sound properly. You don't have to make every event if you don't want to replace the other SFXs listed. Still, please recreate the image in its folder structure, and naming.

BD_chestplate_break

BD_collar_break

BD_faceplate_break

BD_visor_break

dozer_ground_HeadHit

dozer_ground_scratch

dozer_shoulder_shove

dozer_shoulder_tackle

FS_bulldozer_01

We'll come back to these events later.

Now go into the Audio tab, and find the "Actor-Mixer Hierarchy" section.

Under the section should be the Work Unit you imported previously. It'll contain the containers that you import your audio (.wav) files into.

Due to how Wwise handles imports, there are 2 settings that need to be applied for the audio to both work and sound good.

We're editing these Containers:

items.title: Output Bus
items.text:
The first field that needs to be changed is the Output Bus

Click on the 3 dots next to it, and navigate to:

Master-Mixer Hierarchy > Default Work Unit > Master Audio Bus > Main > VO > VO_NPC

Select NPC_System and click OK

items.title: Global Obstruction
items.text:
Next, go into the RTPC tab in the Container Property Editor

This tab will be responsible how much the audio will lower when it comes to walls, doors, and floors being in the way.

Due to how much this is up to you, this is a separate page entirely that can be opened here.

items.title: Audio Importing
items.text:
Importing audio is easy. From file explorer, select the audio you want to use, and drag it onto the respective Container.

A window will open on import settings, for this you want to import it as a Sound SFX. Everything else can be left on its default setting.

If you want a preview of what to expect, Wwise has controls to play, pause, and stop the currently selected container/audio.

Once you're happy with your work, go back to the Events tab.

items.title: Events, again
items.text:
Open the events that were created previously, a window like this should be open:

On the bottom left, there's an option to "Add >>". Click on it, and click "Browse Object..."

Then search for the Container3 that you want to play, whenever this event is triggered.

Once you find it, select and press OK.

Go ahead and do this to the other potential events.

items.title: Disclaimer
items.text:
Unfortunately, there is no way to make Wwise Event mods "natively" on linux. Even with Wine or its forks like Proton.

This is due to Visual Studio 2022, as far as I'm concerned this cannot be "installed" within a Wine environment and have Unreal Engine/Wwise Launcher recognize it.

Currently the "best" way is to install a virtual machine software and set up Windows.

Warning

Unreal Engine requires DirectX support, so not all Virtual Machine software, like VirtualBox, can be used.

VMware currently is the only program that has support for a "Virtual GPU". Maybe at somepoint the program WinBoat can be used instead, when it does get proper Hardware Acceleration support. (last update 9/9/2026)

I am aware of some Virtual Machine software supports GPU Passthrough, though I am not familiar with it and thus will not be covered.

items.title: Hardware Requirements
items.text:
Running another operating system is not a light task, especially for the purpose of our use case.

Officially, the hardware requirements are as follows:

  • 2 CPU cores

  • 8GB of physical memory/RAM

  • 32gb of free storage

Though in reality you are going to need:

  • 6 CPU cores from 2017 (8th gen Intel or 3000 series of Ryzen AMD)

  • 16gb of physical memory/RAM

  • 256gb of free storage

If you are unsure what you have, look up your distro and how you can find your hardware specifications, it's not always universal.

If you don't meet these requirements, I don't recommend you try and run a virtual machine.

items.title: Installing VMware
items.text: Installing VMware depends on what linux distro you use.

items.title: Arch
items.text:
sudo pacman -S vmware-workstation

or

sudo yay -S vmware-workstation

items.title: Linux Other Distros
items.text:
Other distros, like Ubuntu or Fedora, need specific instructions on installing VMware. I do not personally use said distros. My setup uses CachyOS, an Arch based distro.

These resources may be helpful if you do have either installed:

Installing VMWare Workstation Pro on Ubuntu Desktop

How to actually install VMware Workstation on Fedora

VMware Setup

items.title: Windows iso
items.text:
To start, you need either Windows 10 or 11 installation iso.

I recommend Windows 11 (despite how un-epic it is) and the .iso can be acquired here:

Windows 11 iso

If you want, you can technically use Windows 10. That can be acquired here:

Windows 10 iso

items.title: Create New Virutal Machine
items.text:
With VMware open, create a new Virtual Machine

Then do (any option not listed here is fine on the default):

Typical install

Use ISO image > Browse to the previously downloaded iso file.

Name it whatever, and choose where you would want it to be installed. The location does not matter, I recommend it's placed on an SSD drive though.

Enter a password that you can remember, it will autologon for you but do still remember it.

The disk size should be at a minimum 256gb, as you need room for all the software and projects.

items.title: Then customize the hardware:
items.text:
Memory > I recommend you set to half of what you currently have. Meaning if you have 16gb, you should give it 8gb.

Processors > Set the number of processors to 1, and the number of cores to half the amount of threads you have. If you are unsure how many cores/threads you have, look up your processor and see its specification.

Display > Ensure you have "Accelerate 3D Graphics" enabled.

Then close the Machine Settings and Finish.

If the option was enabled, the machine should automatically start for you after clicking Finish.

Windows Setup

items.title: Network issues
items.text:
If you are unable to connect the Virtual Machine to the network, try running this on your Linux OS and try again:

sudo systemctl enable vmware-networks.service

items.title: Skip Microsoft Login
items.text:
Let's get one thing out of the way, you don't want to login into your microsoft account for this. I mean, you're using linux for a reason to begin with.

When Prompted to login, press Shift+F10 on your keyboard. Command prompt should show.

Type in the following: start ms-cxh:localonly and press Enter.

It should prompt you for creating a local account instead.

As well along the way, when prompted for Privacy Settings. Turn all of them off, you don't need any of them.

items.title: Updates and Drivers
items.text:
Go ahead and run Windows and Microsoft Store updates. It might take a while.

Once all updates are installed, you want to install VMware Tools.

At the top bar for VMware, go to VM > install VMware Tools.

It might prompt you to download the Tools, go ahead and do so.

The installer gets mounted as a CD Drive in file explorer.

Right click on it, and click on "Install or run program from your media"

Typical install is what you want. Your screen may flash during install, and it might prompt you to restart the Virtual Machine.

items.title: Debloat
items.text:
There are multiple ways to debloat windows and reduce its size. I do not recommend you use something like Atlas OS AtlasOS.

The tool I recommend you use is Chris Titus Tech's Windows Utility.

You can either use a preset, or go through and choose what you do and do not need.

Generally a lot of windows apps can be removed, like One Drive, Microsoft Edge (if you want to use something else), Microsoft News, Outlook, etc.

items.title: compactos
items.text:
Compactos is a windows command that can compress the base operating system to also reduce size.

Danger

Results can vary with this. Doing this will cost more CPU cycles, and can potentially lead to data loss. Only use this if absolutely needed.

Open CMD as an Admin and enter a command:

To Activate: compact /compactos:always

To Disable: compact /compactos:never

Check Status: compact /compactos:query

Work Setup

items.title: Work Setup
items.text: This section can be skipped if you are already familiar with VMware and its features. Though I can almost deem it necessary for a proper workflow and saving on storage.

items.title: Shared Folders
items.text:
You obiously do not want to install Steam and install another copy of Payday 3 on your system. Especially since VMware can have shared folders between the virtual machine and your operating system.

What I recommend is you make a folder in your Documents (or wherever you find convienent) and name it something fitting for a shared folder.

Turn off the Virtual Machine if it is on. Then in the Virtual Machine settings (Ctrl+D) go to the Options tab, and find Shared Folders.

Make sure it is to be always enabled, and Map as a network drive in Windows guests.

  • Add the folder that was previously created

  • As well add the directory to your installed copy of Payday 3

Info

I personally made the Payday 3 directory read only, to help out potential permission issues in the future. You can make it read/write in this directory if you wish.

Warning

As VMware discloses, this does expose parts of your Linux operating system to windows. Meaning it is more vulnerable to attacks executed on windows.

items.text:
Navigate to Tools from the top, and click New C++ Class

By default, it'll select "None", that's fine.

Click Next>

You can name it whatever you want, then click Create Class

Once this appears, you click OK

When this appears, click No

And now Close Unreal Engine.

Open the Wwise Launcher you previously installed, and navigate to Unreal Engine on the left side

Click on Integrate Wwise in Project... next to the PAYDAY3 project.

Make sure the Integration Version is the one you previously installed:

And under Wwise Project, make sure it points to the previously downloaded project.

Then click Integrate.

Once it's completed, go to your Unreal Engine project in file explorer. By default it's located in Documnets/Unreal Projects

Where the Unreal Engine Project file is, there should be a similarly named .sln next to it.

If you don't see one, right click on the Unreal Engine Project file and click on Generate Visual Studio project files

Open the .sln file by double clicking it, it might prompt what app to use to open the file. Use Microsoft Visual Studio 2022.

Once open, it may give you a temporary guide, just skim through it and you're not required to login.

At the top, you want to click Build then Build Solution (or press Ctrl+Shift+B)

Wait for it to build, you will know if it completed with the purple line turning gray at the bottom.

Once completed, close Visual Studio and re-open your project.

Go into Edit > Project Settings

Scroll all the way to the bottom, and click on Integration Settings

Change the "Root Output Path" with the 3 dots, to the GeneratedSoundBanks folder located in the root of your Wwise Project.

Close Project Settings, and you should see the Wwise Browser on the right hand side.

If you don't see this, go to Window > Wwise Browser

items.title: Epic Games
items.text:
We need a specific version of Unreal Engine. To install Unreal Engine, we need the Epic Games Launcher Epic Games (don’t worry, it won't add Fortnite to your account). Yes, you do need to make an account if you already don’t have one.

While you’re in the Epic Games Launcher, go ahead and claim the free game of the week on the Store tab of the app. You can do this every week, and it is a different game, just a gamer tip.

Info

Optionally, if you don't want to use the Epic Games launcher as an actual game library, you can hide the store and library under settings.

Not shocking at all, it also makes it run faster.

On the top left of the Epic Games Launcher, there will be 3 options. We want to select Unreal Engine.

Then at the top, there will be different tabs. Go ahead and click the “Library” option.

Near where you just clicked, there should be the option to install a new version of UE, click the plus sign and a new UE instance should appear grayed out.

We do not want the latest version of UE, as Payday 3 uses version 5.5.4 as of Update 3.8

To change the version to install, click the version number and a small menu will appear with all the options. Just find 5.5.4 and click on it.

Then click install. A menu might pop up and say where you want to install this, just let it use the default location and click Install.

This might take a while, depending on your internet speed. You can check your install speed with the “Downloads” option in the lower left corner.

Once done, we can move on to Wwise.

items.text:
Download the installer here

Find “Desktop development with C++” and click on it, make sure you have the following checked on the right (it may already be checked by default)

Then go into the Individual Components tab at the top, and search for “4.8”. Then check off the “.NET Framework 4.8 SDK”

items.title: Blank Project or PDML?
items.text:
There are 2 ways making mods at the moment.

  • You can use blank Unreal Engine project and setup Wwise integration manually

    • Doing this will not require the install of the Payday Modloader image/svg+xml image/svg+xml for end-users
    • But will mark you as a modder for online games with the mod installed
    • Uses at a minimum 50 GB of storage

  • Or you can install the Payday Modkit and follow different steps.

    • Doing this will require the install of the Payday Modloader image/svg+xml image/svg+xml for end-users
    • But will not mark you as a modder for online games (as of right now)
    • Uses at a minimum of 80 GB of storage
    • Will also have the benefits of Payday Mod loader such as:
      • In-Game Mod Manager
      • Integrated Mod Settings
      • And more

Note

You could install apps/project files like the Unreal Engine, Wwise Project, and Unreal Projects somewhere other than the C: drive. Though errors you may encounter will require some low-level PC knowledge to be fixed.

Info

Creating custom heist jukebox add-on mods, or next to any jukebox add-on mods, will require the install of the Modkit

If you wish to just use a blank Unreal Engine Project, then continue. If you wish to use the Modkit, then follow the Payday 3 Modding Documentation

Warning

The transition that it comes with, is the default/fallback. Whenever there isn't a dedicated transition, it will use this instead.

You can create more Transitions on the right side.

items.title: Paking
items.text:

Saved > Cooked > WindowsNoEditor > PAYDAY3 > Content > WwiseAudio

If you used Sound SFX or Music Containers, you want to copy Events and Media folders into that Wwise folder in your mod folder

Example:

Half-Life 2 Footsteps > PAYDAY3 > Content > WwiseAudio > Events

Half-Life 2 Footsteps > PAYDAY3 > Content > WwiseAudio > Media

Click on the folder itself, right-click, and click on the option of “Pack with Repak”

Give it some time, and there should be a new file called your [modname].pak

Now you can put this .pak file into your ~mods folder in Papaya 3 and test if you like your mod

PAYDAY3 > Content > Paks > ~mods

items.title: Top to Bottom
items.text:
Payday uses Wwise

Wwise uses Events

Events then Play, Stop, Break, Seek, and more with Containers

Containers then have next to full control on how exactly you want your audio to play and sync with Payday.

We'll start with an example of how a vanilla Event looks (roughly).

The example image shows a rough visual on the overall structure and behaviour of the options and containers. If you want to view it closer, you can right click on the image and open it in a new tab.

Icons

Event

Sequence Container

Random Container

Sound Voice

Audio Bus

Attenuation

Event

The Event in this example does one thing, play the Sequence Container.

The Sequence Container

They play a playlist organized by you. In the example it plays the random containers from 1 to 5, moving on to the next container in the playlist once the current one has concluded.

The Random Container(s)

They play a playlist, though in this case it plays one of them randomly and ends. This is the behaviour by default.

Output Bus

The output bus, for the sake of simplicity, is the assignment of the in-game volume controls.

Listener Relative Routing

3D Spatialization are factors you want to have when audio is playing externally from the player (you). Whether you want Position to be considered, and or Orientation (where the player's camera is facing) to be considered as well.

Speaker Panning/3D Spatialization Mix value is how aggressive do you want the external source to be playing in a speaker direction. For example, stereo has 2 channels/speakers, left and right, having this field at 100 would mean if it is playing in the player's left side would only play on their left ear. Having it at 0 would essentially mean a mono output, where it would play in both channels at equal levels in stereo.

Attenuation

This is only used, at least in our use case, for having distance be considered in lowering the volume when further away from the source. A lot of the time you want to use the value used in-game, which will be provided in the guides.

Diffraction and Transmission

This toggle option does one thing. Whether you want the audio to passthrough walls and floors or not. If you want the audio to respect walls and floors, enable it.

There is a lot to consider when making mods with Wwise, though at the same time it offers almost absolute control for your audio mods in behaviour completely.

You can truly do what you wish in the audio's volume and behaviour using this software. The guides listed on the left is to truly point the path of the Event that plays what you wish to replace, and general guidance for things such as Switches and States. What you do with it and how it behaves is completely up to you.

Using something like Payday Audio Modder image/svg+xml image/svg+xml , means (using the above image as an example) you are replacing the Sound Voice files only. The behaviour being up to what Starbreeze developers chose, not yours.
